_comment: SHARED VECTOR TABLE pinning scripts/skill-union-assert.sh against Fsgg.SkillMirror.verify —
FS-GG/.github#1513, the #398 pattern applied to the second unpinned two-implementation pair.
#120 settled that Fsgg.SkillMirror (FS.GG.Contracts) is ADR-0014's ONE implementation and that the
shell assertion FOLLOWS it. Nothing enforced that claim, and the two diverged three times: the shell
short-circuited check 1 past check 2 (#1506), counted byte-identity without a denominator (#1506),
and short-circuited checks 1-2 past check 3 (#1513). Each was found by a person reading the code,
after it had already misdirected real work.
verify() returns THREE INDEPENDENT FACTS on one SkillDrift record — MissingRoots, Divergent,
HashMismatchRoots — and every vector below states all three, so a shell that can only produce a
SUBSET of them fails a gate instead of being noticed two issues later.
`library` is MEASURED, not transcribed: skillmirror-oracle.sh #loads the library's own source and
runs verify() over these exact vectors. `shell` is what scripts/skill-union-assert.sh must report.
A vector with a `divergence` block is an INTENTIONAL difference between the two implementations, and
it is asserted in BOTH directions (the shell must match `shell`, and `shell` must differ from
`library`) so a documented difference can neither vanish nor silently grow.

residualGap: This block records WHICH library revision the `library` column was measured against. Re-deriving
is a command (`howToRedrive`), and a maintainer holding the library can run it as a check.
A FUTURE LIBRARY CHANGE IS NOW NOTICED, WHICH IT WAS NOT WHEN THIS BLOCK WAS FIRST WRITTEN.
.github#1546 landed scripts/check-skillmirror-freshness.py and the daily
.github/workflows/skillmirror-freshness.yml, which read this block's subject over the API and go
RED when its digest stops matching `skillMirrorFsSha256`. It has found this table dated TWICE:
first .github#1576 (re-derived to `95af075b…`, commit 5debf6e8), then .github#1880, the item
THIS revision was re-derived under.
WHAT THE #1880 RE-DERIVATION MEASURED, stated because a no-op re-derive must be distinguishable
from an unexamined one. The oracle was run against commit bc93f94 (`e44de4a0…`) and NO VECTOR
MOVED: all 10 `fixtures[].library` blocks and all 11 `digestVectors[].digest` values were
reproduced exactly, and the run's only two disagreements were this field and
`digestVectors.measuredAgainst` — the two provenance records this change updates. Because
nothing moved, scripts/skill-union-assert.sh needs no matching correction, and none was made.
The span 5debf6e8..bc93f94 is 31 commits wide. It leaves Schemas.fs untouched across all of
them and touches SkillMirror.fs in exactly two, both ADDITIVE at the surface this table
measures:
* da07830 (FS.GG.SDD#737/#749, the byte seam) appends `BodyRefusalReason`, `decodeBody` and
`sha256Bytes`, leaving `sha256` itself untouched.
* bc93f94 (FS.GG.SDD#760, the third observation state) refactors `verifyFiles` and
`verifyFileSet` onto private cores taking an unobserved-subject index, and adds
`verifyObservedFiles`/`verifyObservedFileSet`. Both public spellings are re-expressed as
their core with an EMPTY index, which is the pre-#760 behaviour by construction.
NEITHER touches `verify`, the single-body entry point the `fixtures` column measures, nor
`sha256`, which the `digestVectors` column measures — so both columns reproducing was the
expected outcome, and the oracle run is what turned that expectation into a measurement.
TWO SPANS WERE MEASURED, NOT ONE, and the intermediate one is recorded because it was real: the
re-derive first ran against 58a14144 — the head when the item was CLAIMED, and the last one
still carrying `20fdb35c…`, the digest #1880 recorded — and FS.GG.SDD's default branch moved to
bc93f94 mid-item. (58a14144 postdates the issue by four hours; it is NOT the head #1880 was
filed against. The issue pinned a DIGEST, and that digest was current from da07830 through
58a14144.) Both runs reproduced every vector; only the later is recorded above, because the gate
grades the DEFAULT BRANCH and a provenance record naming a superseded head would red the moment
it landed.
THAT RACE IS THIS TABLE'S STANDING COST, not a defect of this change. The provenance is a
revision pin against a repository that moves independently, so any library commit landing after
this one reds the gate again and asks for another oracle run. Nothing here can close that; it is
the tripwire working.
IT IS A TRIPWIRE, NOT A PROOF OF ALIGNMENT, AND THIS TABLE IS NOT SELF-MAINTAINING. The gate
compares a digest of ONE file, so it can say the library MOVED and can never say whether the
move altered `verify`'s behaviour — only re-running the oracle answers that. And `Schemas.fs`,
which the oracle also `#load`s, is outside the gate's reach (.github#1577), so a change confined
there moves `verify` while the gate stays green. One such change is already inside the span
re-derived here: `Schemas.fs` took `skillManifestVersion` from 1 to 2 (FS.GG.SDD#727), and no
digest this gate watches covered that line. The oracle `#load`s both files, so THIS
re-derivation did cover it; the gate would not have.
Stated in brief and deliberately NOT restated in full: the whole account lives in
docs/coordination/skill-union-assertion.md, 'What pins #120's alignment claim'. A third copy of
it would be one more thing to drift.

bodies._comment: Named once so a vector's `bodies` map and its `sha256` cannot drift apart by a typo.

_comment: THE THREE-WAY DIGEST TABLE — FS-GG/.github#1547. The `fixtures` array above pins `verify`'s
three FACTS across two implementations; this pins the DIGEST across all THREE, which is the
surface #1547 exists because nobody covered.
WHAT WAS UNCOVERED. The canonical skill digest has three implementations —
`Fsgg.SkillMirror.sha256` (the library, ADR-0014's one implementation), `skill_digest` in
scripts/skill-union-assert.sh, and `canonical_digest` in scripts/fsgg-skill-registry-check —
and they were pinned PAIRWISE by two mechanisms that both skipped the digest: conformance.sh
pins shell<->Python for the PREDICATE GRAMMAR only, and skillmirror-conformance.sh pinned
shell<->library for the THREE FACTS. Nothing anywhere ran one input through all three. CRLF is
the instance that surfaced (the library folded it, the two shells did not); the uncovered
surface was the finding.
THE DECISION (2026-07-27, recorded on #1547): align the two shells to the library. Both now
strip a leading UTF-8 BOM and fold CRLF->LF before hashing. CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN
INFERRED: a CRLF file and its LF twin now hash IDENTICALLY, so the digest checks are
deliberately slightly more permissive than a byte comparison. Cross-root byte-identity
(`divergent`) is untouched and still separates them.
ONE EXPECTED VALUE PER VECTOR, NOT THREE COLUMNS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. `digest` is what all
three must return. There is deliberately no per-implementation column and no `divergence`
escape hatch here: re-introducing a disagreement cannot be done by editing one side's column,
it requires changing the single value every side is measured against — which the oracle then
rejects unless the LIBRARY moved. That is the asymmetry ADR-0014 asserts, expressed in the
table's shape instead of in a comment.
`bytesBase64`, NOT A JSON STRING LITERAL. These vectors turn on a leading BOM, on lone CRs and
on exact trailing bytes — precisely the things an editor, a linter or a careless re-serialize
silently normalizes away. base64 makes the input bytes reviewable and tamper-evident, and
removes any question about what a `\uFEFF` in a JSON string is supposed to encode.
PROVENANCE. `digest` is MEASURED, exactly like the `library` column above: skillmirror-oracle.sh
decodes each vector, hands the body to the library's own `SkillMirror.sha256`, and reports any
vector whose recorded value differs. skillmirror-conformance.sh then drives the two SHELLS over
the same bytes hermetically, on every PR, via their `--digest` reference seams.
EVERY VECTOR IS VALID UTF-8, AND THAT BOUNDARY IS DELIBERATE. The canonical digest is defined
over decoded text, while the in-repo shells hash raw bytes; those implementations therefore do not
claim an invalid-byte digest in common. FS.GG.Contracts now REFUSES a body that does not decode at
its read seam, with a distinct diagnostic, before it reaches SkillMirror.sha256. An invalid body
has no expected digest by design, so this table records exactly one expected value only for the
valid-UTF-8 domain where all implementations are meaningfully comparable (.github#1656).
A SEPARATE PROVENANCE RECORD FOR A SEPARATE MEASURED COLUMN. `derivedFrom` names the revision
the `fixtures[].library` column was measured at; this names the revision the
`digestVectors[].digest` column was measured at. They name the SAME revision today —
.github#1880 re-derived both in one oracle run — and they are still two fields, because the
two columns can be re-derived independently, and stamping one under the other's record is
exactly how a table comes to assert a measurement nobody made.
THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: THEY HAVE ALREADY DIFFERED. When this block was added (.github#1547)
`derivedFrom` was stale at `b1c7e94d…` (commit a066e0bc) while these digests were measured at
`2742eb73…`, and #1547 correctly declined to rewrite a field it had not itself re-derived.
#1576 then re-ran the oracle against `95af075b…` (commit 5debf6e8) and reconciled both, and
#1880 re-ran it against `e44de4a0…` (commit bc93f94) and reconciled both again. All 11
`digest` values below were reproduced UNCHANGED by that run; only this provenance record
moved.
THE ORACLE ENFORCES THIS BLOCK'S PRESENCE, not just its value: a `digest` column carrying no
record of what it was measured against is a measurement no reader can locate, so
skillmirror-oracle.fsx reports a missing `measuredAgainst` as a DISAGREEMENT.

vectors.name: lf
vectors.note: The base case: an LF-authored, BOM-free body. Every other vector is this one perturbed, and they all collapse onto its digest except where a lone CR survives.

vectors.name: crlf
vectors.note: #1547's subject. The SAME logical body on a CRLF checkout. Its digest equals `lf`'s — that equality IS the decision, and before #1547 the two shells disagreed with the library here.

vectors.name: bom-lf
vectors.note: A leading UTF-8 BOM must not enter the digest (.github#384). The library's callers decode as UTF-8 and the decoder consumes it; both shells strip it explicitly. Equals `lf`.

vectors.name: bom-crlf
vectors.note: BOTH normalizations at once, which is the combination a Windows editor actually produces. Equals `lf`. An implementation that applied only one of the two would fail HERE and pass `bom-lf` and `crlf` individually — which is why the combination is a vector and not an assumption.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.note: An empty body. `SkillMirror.sha256` special-cases null/empty to "", which is the same value the general path would produce, so the vector pins that the special case is a no-op rather than a second behaviour. This is sha256 of zero bytes.

vectors.name: lone-cr
vectors.note: THE ANTI-`tr -d '\r'` VECTOR. The library replaces the two-byte PAIR CR LF, not the CHARACTER CR, so a bare CR inside a line SURVIVES and this digest differs from `lf`'s. The obvious shell fix — piping through `tr -d '\r'` — passes `crlf` and fails here, which is exactly why the obvious fix is wrong.

vectors.name: cr-cr-lf
vectors.note:
`a
b
`. Exactly ONE pair is folded, leaving `a
b
` — so an implementation that folds repeatedly until no CR remains, or that scans right-to-left, lands somewhere else. Pins that the fold is a single non-overlapping pass, the semantics of .NET's String.Replace.

vectors.name: trailing-lone-cr
vectors.note: THE FAIL-OPEN THIS TABLE EXISTS TO CATCH. `# beta skill\r`, a trailing CR with no LF. Under `tr -d '\r'` this hashes IDENTICALLY to `no-trailing-newline` below — two distinct files sharing one digest, which is a missed drift (#266) rather than a spurious one. Under the library, and now under both shells, they differ.

vectors.name: no-trailing-newline
vectors.note: A body with no final newline. Its own digest, and the partner `trailing-lone-cr` must not collide with.

vectors.name: nul-byte
vectors.note: `a\0b\r\nc\n`. THE VECTOR THAT CAUGHT A FAIL-OPEN THIS ITEM ITSELF SHIPPED (.github#1547). The first cut of `skill_digest` slurped the body with `$(cat …)`, and bash DISCARDS NUL bytes in a command substitution — so `a\0b` and `ab` hashed IDENTICALLY while the library and the Python checker told them apart: two distinct files, one digest, a MISSED drift. The fold is now streamed through `sed -z`, where NUL is a record separator and every byte survives. A shell implementation that goes back to slurping fails HERE and passes all nine other vectors.

vectors.name: many-trailing-lf
vectors.note:
`# beta skill


`. Pins that trailing newlines are COUNTED, which is a live hazard for a shell implementation specifically: `$(cat f)` strips every trailing newline, so a `skill_digest` written without the `printf x` sentinel collapses this onto `lf` and reports a matching digest for a file that does not match.

fixtures.name: whole-and-coherent-and-matching
fixtures.note: The all-clean case. verify() returns NOTHING for it, so all three facts are empty.

fixtures.name: whole-and-coherent-but-digest-mismatched
fixtures.note: Every root holds the same body and none of them matches the manifest. HashMismatchRoots names EVERY root, not one representative — the per-root shape this vector exists to pin.

fixtures.name: partitioned-but-matching
fixtures.note: A partition of copies that DO match the manifest. The digest fact must stay empty — a partition may not manufacture a drift, which is the #1506 lesson pointed the other way.

fixtures.name: partitioned-AND-digest-mismatched
fixtures.note: THE #1513 DEFECT, measured on main at 22461b4: an id that is BOTH partitioned AND digest-mismatched. The shell reported only [partitioned]; the library returns both facts on the same record. This is the vector that fails against the pre-fix script.

fixtures.name: partitioned-AND-divergent-AND-digest-mismatched
fixtures.note: All three facts true at once, which no short-circuiting implementation can express. Both present copies differ from each other and from the manifest.

fixtures.name: divergent-and-the-REFERENCE-root-is-the-clean-one
fixtures.note: THE VECTOR THAT DECIDES per-root vs representative-root, and it decides it as a FAIL-OPEN. Two roots match the manifest and the third has drifted. A digest taken from the first present root (.claude) matches, so a representative-root check reports NO mismatch at all and .agents' drift is invisible. HashMismatchRoots names .agents. This is #266's shape: a check that was not made, rendered as a check that passed.

fixtures.name: divergent-and-the-REFERENCE-root-is-the-drifted-one
fixtures.note: The same tree with the drift moved onto the reference root. A representative-root check gets the right VERDICT here by luck and still cannot say WHICH root drifted — and it is the same code path that fails open in the vector above.

fixtures.name: no-reference-digest-skips-the-hash-fact-only
fixtures.note: An empty Sha256 means 'no reference digest' (SkillMirror.fsi, ExpectedSkill). The hash fact is skipped; presence and cross-root identity still hold. Pinned so a blank digest can never be read as a passing digest.

fixtures.name: crlf-body-against-an-lf-digest-AGREES
fixtures.note: WAS the KNOWN-DIVERGENCE vector, and is now an agreement vector — .github#1547. SkillMirror.sha256 replaces CRLF with LF BEFORE hashing (feature 070, so an LF-authored body does not spuriously drift on a Windows checkout); the shell's skill_digest and the Python canonical_digest did NOT, so a CRLF checkout produced a spurious [drifted] the library never reported. The 2026-07-27 decision on #1547 aligned BOTH shells to the library — ADR-0014 names the library the one implementation and #120 records that the shells follow it, so the shells were the drifted copies. `hashMismatchRoots` is therefore now EMPTY here, equal to the library, and this vector's job flipped from pinning a difference to pinning its ABSENCE: if either shell ever stops folding CRLF, this vector reds. The digest-level triple is pinned separately and per-implementation by `digestVectors` below.

fixtures.name: KNOWN-DIVERGENCE-declared-but-absent-from-every-root
fixtures.note: verify() iterates the EXPECTED (manifest) set, so an id materialized nowhere is drift with MissingRoots = every root. The shell iterates the ON-DISK union, so such an id is not a union member at all and reaches the manifest-to-disk sweep instead: without --params it is the superset catalog's legitimate 'declared-absent' (#120), and with --params and a true condition it is [missing] (ADR-0017). The two implementations answer different questions here and both are right; asserting it stops the difference being rediscovered as a bug.

divergence.direction: shell is LOOSER, by design (#120 superset-catalog semantics)
divergence.why: The manifest is an upper bound: emission is lifecycle/profile-conditioned, so declared-and-absent-everywhere is legitimate without --params. ADR-0017's --params turns it into [missing] when the condition is true.
divergence.decision: settled by #120 and ADR-0017; asserted here so it stays a decision rather than an accident.
